paper.title_en: What Is the Maximum Density of Microwave Control Lines in a Superconducting Quantum Computer?
paper.abstract_en: Scaling up superconducting quantum computers requires denser control wiring, introducing microwave crosstalk along the entire cryogenic signal path rather than only near the chip. Here, we introduce a framework that combines microwave transmission-line theory with a quantum Hamiltonian description to quantify the wiring-induced microwave crosstalk and the resulting gate infidelity for an all-microwave universal gate set. Using this approach, we determine the equal-level far-end crosstalk (ELFEXT) required to operate fixed-frequency transmons at arbitrary target fidelities and find that achieving 99.99% fidelity requires ELFEXT levels of approximately <math display="inline"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>43</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>dB</mi></mrow></math> for the <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> gate and <math display="inline"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>73</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>dB</mi></mrow></math> for the cross-resonance gate. Finally, we use these results to bound the number of physical qubits on a chip.
